key_insight: Perovskite-based tandem photovoltaics can support terawatt-scale clean energy only if circular design and end-of-life recovery are built in from the start.
engineering_relevance: The review highlights practical engineering priorities for commercialization: replacing scarce materials, enabling low-cost delamination and recycling, and safely managing lead across the device lifecycle.
method: Synthesizes materials, technoeconomic, and policy considerations for circular PV design.
Identifies key bottlenecks in recycling, stack separation, and lead sequestration.
Outlines strategies to co-optimize device performance with sustainability and circularity.
evidence_signal: The abstract is a review that draws on lifecycle and technoeconomic perspectives, including the projected 160 million tonnes of c-Si PV waste by 2050, rather than reporting new experimental performance data.
watch_item: Circularity claims depend on scalable, validated recycling and lead-containment processes that are not yet fully established at commercial scale.
paper_title: Circularity in Perovskite-Based Tandem Photovoltaics for Terawatt-Scale Deployment
